composer.answer: Project Orchid chose not to use Redis because adding and operating another stateful service would create unnecessary operational complexity and ownership cost; the decision was not based on Redis being technically poor (S009). Redis had been considered for low-latency distributed locks, pending an Operations assessment of whether another stateful service was justified (S007). The later lock-contention test did not reverse the decision: it used an intentionally unrealistic burst at roughly 20 times expected first-release load, and the note explicitly says it does not reverse the no-Redis decision (S010).

composer.answer: INC-77 began at 09:12 on April 14, when database CPU was saturated and latency rising; the initial database-capacity explanation was explicitly unconfirmed (S011). By 09:25, increased retries and queue depth were linked to the timeout configuration rollout, pausing retries reduced CPU, and rollback began (S012). The final assessment identified a retry storm caused by that rollout, with database saturation as a downstream symptom, superseding the early hypothesis (S013). The April 17 addendum changed only the previously circulated start time—from 09:10 to the corrected 09:12 based on the source log—and did not change the root-cause assessment (S014).

composer.answer: No. Redis was rejected for the first release because of operational complexity and the burden of owning another stateful service, not because it was considered technically poor (S009).
